notes: The wiring diagram is treated as the authority. It shows red LED on GPIO25, amber on GPIO8 and green on GPIO7 (the diagram's 'GP' labels follow the standard 40-pin header). The text's 28 and 27 are BCM numbers the diagram does not show, so I did not use them. Button is on GPIO21 and buzzer on GPIO15, matching the text.
The Pi header sockets/pins are modelled with the catalogue 'raspberry-pi' type. The black GND wire goes to the GND pin in the right-hand column, third row (physical pin 6), named GND.1.
Pi-to-breadboard jumpers are modelled as male-to-female wires, with port a on the female (Pi) end and b on the male (breadboard) end. The button-to-rail wire is a plain male-to-male jumper-wire.

The right-hand power rail, which acts as GND, is named with 'tp.<n>' holes. The catalogue's rail-to-edge mapping is unclear, and every hole on one rail is the same strip. Different n values were used for each insertion point (tp.2 wire1, tp.6 buzzer, tp.9/16/22 LED cathodes, tp.29 button wire).

Resistors span the centre gap from column e (top bank) to column h (bottom bank). Each LED anode is in column j on the resistor's row, and its cathode goes to the GND rail. The curved (longer) leg is assumed to be the anode.
The buzzer's '+' leg is in row 4 column j, on the same strip as the blue GPIO15 wire (4b.g). It is mapped to port 1, and port 2 goes to the GND rail.

The button straddles the centre gap in rows 28 and 30. Its top pair of legs (side 1) is on row 28 and connects to GND via the black wire at 28t.d. Its bottom pair (side 2) is on row 30 and connects to GPIO21 via the purple wire at 30t.d. The right-hand legs sit in the bottom bank with no wire attached. No external pull resistor is drawn, so the software would use the Pi's internal pull-up.
Resistor values are not given in the manual, so 220 ohm is assumed.
